title: Claude Managed Agents
content:
## What Are Managed Agents?

Claude Managed Agents is an Anthropic-hosted service that runs persistent, long-horizon agentic workflows on your behalf. Unlike the raw API — where you send a prompt and receive a response — Managed Agents maintains session state across days or weeks, can spawn sub-agents, and operates in the background without an active user session.

Key distinction: the API gives you a model; Managed Agents gives you a running process.

---

## Dreaming

Introduced in May 2026, "dreaming" extends an agent's memory by having it review past sessions to identify patterns and incrementally update its own behavior guidelines.

How it works:
1. After completing a session, the agent writes a structured reflection of what succeeded, what failed, and what heuristics to carry forward.
2. Those reflections are stored in a per-agent memory store.
3. At the start of subsequent sessions, the relevant memories are surfaced in the system prompt.

The practical effect: an agent that repeatedly runs a weekly reporting workflow learns over time which data sources are unreliable, which stakeholders prefer which formats, and which edge cases need special handling — without any manual prompt tuning.

---

## Multi-Agent Orchestration

A lead agent can decompose a task and delegate each sub-task to a specialist agent with its own model, system prompt, and tool set. Specialists run in parallel on a shared filesystem, then the lead merges results.

Example configuration:
```json
{
  "orchestrator": {
    "model": "claude-opus-4-7",
    "prompt": "You are the project lead. Break work into sub-tasks and delegate."
  },
  "specialists": [
    { "id": "researcher", "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "tools": ["web_search"] },
    { "id": "coder",      "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "tools": ["code_execution"] },
    { "id": "reviewer",  "model": "claude-haiku-4-5",  "tools": [] }
  ]
}
```

Specialists share read/write access to a common workspace directory; the orchestrator reads their outputs and synthesizes a final result.

---

## MCP Tunnels

MCP tunnels let Managed Agents route traffic to MCP servers inside a private network, without exposing those servers to the public internet.

Use cases:
- Reach an internal Postgres database as a tool
- Connect to a private REST API or knowledge base
- Access ticketing or incident-management systems (Jira, PagerDuty) behind a corporate firewall

Setup: deploy the `anthropic-mcp-tunnel` sidecar in your VPC; configure the agent to connect via the tunnel endpoint. Traffic is encrypted end-to-end, and the sidecar authenticates with your identity provider.

---

## Self-Hosted Sandboxes

For teams with strict data-residency or compliance requirements, Managed Agents supports self-hosted sandboxes: the agent's code-execution and file-system operations run inside compute you control (AWS, GCP, or on-prem), while Anthropic's infrastructure handles only model inference.

---

## Webhooks and Background Automation

Managed Agents exposes a webhook endpoint per agent. POST a payload to trigger a run; the agent starts asynchronously, completes the task, and calls your configured callback URL with the result.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/agents/{agent_id}/runs \
  -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"input": "Generate the weekly executive summary from last 7 days of Slack.",
       "callback_url": "https://your-system.internal/hooks/agent-done"}'
```

Combined with dreaming and multi-agent orchestration, this pattern enables fully autonomous pipelines that self-improve over time without human intervention in the loop.

---

## Pricing and Availability

Managed Agents is available on Claude Enterprise and select paid plans. Pricing is based on session-minutes and model tier, separate from per-token API charges. MCP tunnels and self-hosted sandboxes are add-ons available to enterprise customers.
